newsitem.title: UK: Conservative support slumps in Scotland - poll.
newsitem.headline: Conservative support slumps in Scotland - poll.

text.p: Conservative support in Scotland has slumped to just over half the general election level which saw the party lose all its Scottish seats, according to the latest opinion poll.

A System Three poll published in the Herald newspaper on Tuesday put Conservative support at 10 percent, two points down on the month and eight points below its May election vote. Labour was steady on 54 percent, eight points up on its general election vote.
The monthly poll found the Scottish National Party up one since July at 24 percent. Liberal Democrats were down one to nine percent.
Britain's Labour government is holding a referendum in September for Scots to decide if they want their own parliament again, 290 years after it was united with the English parliament at Westminster.
The poll shows 87 percent of Scots are in favour.
It was carried out in 39 of Scotland's 72 constituencies from July 24 to July 29, after the Labour government published details of the powers proposed for a devolved Scottish parliament.
Conservatives are the only party campaigning against change. They say a separate parliament would lead to the break-up of the United Kingdom.
